paras_en: Key points:

The yen has rebounded strongly – is this time genuine? Market bets on rate hikes are heating up, and the focus now shifts to U.S. employment data. The yen appreciated sharply from over ¥160 per dollar to around ¥157 within two trading days. The upcoming U.S. jobs report on Friday will determine whether this yen reversal has further upside potential.

The yen finally found upward momentum. On Thursday, USD/JPY dropped 1% below ¥157, hitting its lowest level in about a month. After a 0.9% rise on Wednesday, the yen turned a seemingly failed defense of the ¥160 level into a notable two‑day reversal. The yen had earlier touched the 40‑year low near ¥164, prompting a rare joint intervention by the U.S. and Japan that pushed USD/JPY down to ¥155.20, though most of the rally was later given back. The latest yen rise appears driven by shifting rate expectations rather than merely government dollar sales. Earlier speculation that Japanese authorities might intervene again or conduct a “rate check” (officials asking banks for real‑time quotes before formal intervention) is giving way to analysts attributing the move to hawkish signals from the Bank of Japan. This time the yen may have truly found its fuel.
The Bank of Japan is turning more hawkish. Governor Kazuo Ueda’s deputy, Takada Sō, said rates should be adjusted flexibly according to inflation rather than following a predictable twice‑a‑year hike schedule. BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda noted that economic and price risks will be discussed at the September meeting, meaning each policy meeting could become a rate‑hike opportunity. The market has almost fully priced in a rate hike this month and expects about 50 basis points of cumulative hikes by year‑end. One basis point equals one‑hundredth of a percent. Japan’s two‑year government bond yield rose to 1.83% on Wednesday, the highest since 1995. Higher Japanese yields reduce the appeal of carry trades—borrowing yen at low rates to invest in higher‑yielding overseas assets. If the BOJ accelerates hikes, the profit space for such positions shrinks, prompting traders to unwind and buy back yen, turning the world’s favorite funding currency into one that now carries an “entry fee”.
U.S. non‑farm payrolls will decide the other side’s direction. Friday’s U.S. jobs report is expected to show about 56,000 new jobs. The market currently sees a roughly 60% chance of a Fed rate hike in September. Weak employment data could cool hike expectations, lower U.S. bond yields, and push USD/JPY further down. Strong payrolls and wage growth could support Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s hawkish stance and lift USD/JPY back to ¥159 or even ¥160. The current exchange‑rate move essentially reflects a re‑pricing battle between two rate expectations: a faster BOJ tightening versus a possible further Fed hike. Key levels to watch: ¥157 is a short‑term pivot, with support near ¥156 and the post‑intervention low of ¥155.20. Resistance lies at ¥159‑¥160. A break below ¥157.50 would reinforce a bearish USD/long‑yen reversal, while a return to ¥160 would suggest the yen’s rally still needs official “assist”.

paras: 美元周四(3日)下跌，創逾兩周來最差單日表現，主要因美國公債殖利率下滑及日元強勁反彈。
紐約尾盤，追蹤美元兌六種主要貨幣的美元指數(DXY)下跌0.7%，報98.91。
美國公債殖利率下滑拖累美元。交易員在美債經歷一波劇烈拋售後開始逢低買進，帶動殖利率回落。美國10年期公債殖利率周二升至2023年11月以來最高，周四最新下跌3.3個基點至4.761%。
固定收益市場近期的拋售潮，主要受到多項因素推動，包括高油價引發的通膨疑慮、企業為建置AI基礎設施而大舉舉債可能造成的債務不可持續疑慮，以及政府財政債務持續膨脹。
聯準會理事華勒(Christopher Waller)釋出的一些正面訊息，也有助於改善市場情緒。
華勒在接受Reuters NEXT訪問時準備的談話稿中表示，「雖然通膨仍明顯高於聯邦公開市場委員會(FOMC)設定的2%目標，但近期數據顯示，我們終於看到一些通膨降溫的跡象。如果未來兩周公布的數據持續呈現這種趨勢，我將傾向支持維持聯邦資金利率目前的水準。」
這名FOMC投票委員補充，他認為潛在通膨的表現其實遠優於核心通膨數據所呈現的情況。相較於聯準會主席華許(Kevin Warsh)上周在傑克森霍爾(Jackson Hole)年度央行會議上的演講，華勒此次發言的語氣較不偏鷹。
Macquarie外匯與利率策略師Thierry Wizman表示，「如果目前主要央行再次形成一個共同趨勢，那就是貨幣政策應對供給衝擊引發的新一波通膨保持戒心。這可能是過去兩周聯準會、歐洲央行(ECB)、澳洲央行(RBA)、加拿大央行(BoC)及日本銀行紛紛採取較為鷹派立場時，最明確且最普遍的考量因素。」
「如果所有央行同時轉向鷹派，對外匯市場的影響仍難以確定。但在油價高漲的背景下，我們仍偏好美元相較於澳幣、歐元及英鎊的表現，原因在於稀缺石油的貿易條件優勢有利於美國。」
日元飆至1個月高點
日元周四成為外匯市場焦點。日元強勁反彈，兌美元一度升至155.30，創8月3日以來最高，當時距離美日當局歷史性聯手干預匯市僅數日。包括這次具里程碑意義的聯合干預在內，日本從7月30日至8月26日合計動用創紀錄的15兆日元來支撐日元。
日元本周稍早一度貶破160日元兌1美元，這被視為東京當局密切關注的關鍵干預水準。雖然周四沒有任何干預行動獲得證實，但投資人間的相關揣測甚囂塵上。
布魯金斯研究院資深經濟研究員Robin Brooks表示，「日元隔夜的升值走勢具干預的所有典型特徵：日元急劇、垂直式升值，但日美利差並未同步擴大，無法從水準面解釋這樣的升幅。如果看起來像干預，那就是干預。」
除了可能的干預行動之外，本周日本銀行(BoJ)決策官員釋出的偏鷹訊號，也為日元提供支撐。
美國財政部長貝森特(Scott Bessent)周日在北卡羅來納州舉行的G20會議期間，與日銀總裁植田和男(Kazuo Ueda)會面。貝森特當時「強烈支持日本採取果斷的市場與貨幣政策措施，以因應日元被大幅低估的問題」。
植田周二在一場會議上證實，日銀將在9月討論升息，此外，日銀委員高田創(Hajime Takata)進一步強化市場的升息預期，主張採取更靈活的升息路徑。

paras_en: The dollar fell on Thursday (the 3rd), posting its worst single‑day performance in over two weeks, mainly due to a drop in U.S. Treasury yields and a strong rebound in the yen.
In the New York close, the dollar index (DXY), which tracks the greenback against six major currencies, slipped 0.7% to 98.91.

Falling U.S. Treasury yields weighed on the dollar. After a sharp sell‑off in Treasuries, traders began buying on dips, pushing yields lower. The 10‑year U.S. Treasury yield, which had risen on Tuesday to its highest since November 2023, fell 3.3 basis points on Thursday to 4.761%.

The recent bond‑market sell‑off has been driven by several factors, including inflation worries sparked by high oil prices, concerns that corporate borrowing to build AI infrastructure could become unsustainable, and the continued expansion of government fiscal debt.
Positive remarks from Fed Governor Christopher Waller also helped improve market sentiment.

In a prepared statement for a Reuters NEXT interview, Waller said, "Although inflation remains clearly above the Federal Open Market Committee’s 2% target, recent data show that we are finally seeing some signs of cooling. If the data released over the next two weeks continue this trend, I would be inclined to support keeping the federal funds rate at its current level."

The voting FOMC member added that he believes underlying inflation is actually performing far better than core‑inflation figures suggest. Compared with Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s speech at the Jackson Hole annual central‑bank meeting last week, Waller’s tone was less hawkish.

Macquarie FX and rates strategist Thierry Wizman said, "If the major central banks are again forming a common trend, it is that monetary policy should remain cautious toward a new wave of inflation triggered by supply shocks. This has been the clearest and most common consideration over the past two weeks as the Fed, ECB, RBA, BoC and BOJ have all taken relatively hawkish stances."

"If all central banks turn hawkish at the same time, the impact on FX markets is still uncertain. But against a backdrop of high oil prices, we still prefer the dollar over the Australian, euro and pound, because the trade‑flow advantage of scarce oil benefits the United States," he added.
The yen surged to a one‑month high

The yen became the focus of the FX market on Thursday, rallying sharply and briefly reaching 155.30 per dollar, the highest level since August 3, just days after historic joint intervention by U.S. and Japanese authorities. Including this landmark coordinated intervention, Japan used a record 15 trillion yen from July 30 to August 26 to support the currency.

Earlier this week the yen had slipped past 160 per dollar, a level viewed by Tokyo as a key threshold for intervention. No intervention was confirmed on Thursday, but speculation among investors was rampant.

Brookings senior economist Robin Brooks said, "The yen’s overnight appreciation shows all the hallmarks of intervention: a rapid, vertical move while the U.S.–Japan rate differential did not widen, making the rise impossible to explain on fundamentals alone. If it looks like intervention, it is intervention."
In addition to possible intervention, hawkish signals from Bank of Japan policymakers this week also gave the yen support.

U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent met BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda during the G20 meeting in North Carolina on Sunday. Bessent said he "strongly supports Japan taking decisive market and monetary‑policy actions to address the yen’s significant undervaluation."

Ueda confirmed on Tuesday at a meeting that the BOJ will discuss a rate hike in September, and BOJ board member Hajime Takata further reinforced market expectations for tightening, advocating a more flexible path for future hikes.
Among other major currencies, the euro rose 0.4% against the dollar to $1.1632.
Even though Eurostat data showed a 1.6% month‑on‑month increase in July industrial producer prices in the euro area, the euro kept climbing, contrasting with a 0.3% decline in June.
Markets are awaiting the European Central Bank’s rate decision next week, with consensus expecting a 25‑basis‑point hike.
The Canadian dollar strengthened versus the dollar, with the USD/CAD pair down 0.4% at 1.3787.

paras: 台北股匯今(3)日走勢震盪，台股尾盤賣壓出籠收黑，新台幣兌美元先升後貶，一度摜破 31.8 元關卡，並未跟隨日元等亞幣走強，在央行出手調節下，終場貶勢收斂，收在 31.755 元，貶值 2.7 分，為連 2 黑，台北與元太外匯市場總成交值萎縮至 27.31 億美元。
新台幣兌美元今天開盤價為 31.75 元，早盤最高升抵 31.70 元，但隨著熱錢流出，匯價最低來到 31.827 元，所幸尾盤靠央行介入穩匯，驚險收復 31.8 元關卡，以 31.755 元作收，貶值 2.7 分。
美伊緊張局勢升溫，再度掀起升息疑慮，台股今天尾盤急殺 307 點，失守46000點關卡，收在 45857.66 點，台積電、聯發科表現有撐，但記憶體、PCB 等電子族群賣壓沉重。三大法人合計賣超637.11億元，其中外資及陸資賣超481.46億元。
觀察主要亞幣今天對美元表現，日元強勢大漲 1.62%，韓元同步勁揚0.66%，星幣升值 0.33%，人民幣升值 0.06%，新台幣走勢獨憔悴，收盤下挫 0.09%。
日元日前一度貶破 160 兌 1 美元大關，隨後於 2 日急升至 158 字頭。隨著美國財長貝森特(Scott Bessent)近期公開敦促日本升息，市場人士解讀，160 關卡可能已成為美方與日本央行(BOJ)共同防守的新底線。日銀將於 9 月 17 日至 18 日召開貨幣政策會議，總裁植田和男面臨進退兩難局面，而市場目前已高度反映本月升息 1 碼的預期。
paras_en: Taipei's stock and FX markets were volatile today (the 3rd), with the Taiwan index ending the session in the red under selling pressure. The New Taiwan dollar rose against the US dollar before falling, briefly breaking the 31.8 level, and did not follow the rally in the yen and other Asian currencies. After the central bank intervened, the depreciation eased and the dollar closed at 31.755, down 2.7 cents, marking a second consecutive red day. Total turnover in the Taipei and Yuan‑Tai foreign‑exchange markets shrank to $2.731 billion.

The New Taiwan dollar opened at 31.75 per US dollar, climbed to a high of 31.70 in early trading, but as hot money fled, the rate fell to a low of 31.827. Fortunately, central‑bank intervention near the close steadied the market, narrowly reclaiming the 31.8 barrier and finishing at 31.755, down 2.7 cents.

Rising US‑Iran tensions revived rate‑hike concerns, and the Taiwan index plunged 307 points in the final session, slipping below the 46,000 mark to close at 45,857.66. TSMC and MediaTek provided some support, but memory‑chip, PCB and other electronics sectors faced heavy selling. The three major institutional investors sold a combined NT$63.711 billion, with foreign and mainland investors accounting for NT$48.146 billion of the net outflow.

Looking at the performance of major Asian currencies against the dollar, the yen surged 1.62%, the won rose 0.66%, the Singapore dollar appreciated 0.33%, the renminbi gained 0.06%, while the New Taiwan dollar was the only one to weaken, closing down 0.09%.

The yen had briefly slipped past the 160 per dollar threshold before rallying sharply to the 158 range on the 2nd. After US Treasury official Scott Bessent publicly urged Japan to raise rates, market participants read that the 160 level may now serve as a new joint floor defended by the US and the Bank of Japan. The BOJ is set to hold its monetary policy meeting on September 17‑18, with Governor Kazuo Ueda facing a dilemma, and markets have already priced in a one‑percentage‑point rate hike this month.

items.title: 日元飛速飆升 日銀本次並未大規模干預 空軍畏戰主動平倉
items.title_en: Yen Soars Rapidly; BOJ Does Not Intervene on a Large Scale; Traders Fear Intervention and Close Shorts
paras: 日元兌美元匯率周三(2日)與周四出現強烈波動，走勢自 160.38 快速升值並突破 158 關卡，盤中甚至一度創下近一個月新高 156.36。這波急劇漲勢迅速引發市場熱議，猜測日本政府是否再度出手干預匯市。
然而，日本央行(BOJ)公布的經常帳數據顯示，本周並無大規模干預的跡象。市場分析指出，此波行情並非官方直接干預，而是由交易員對央行升息預期的「重新定價」以及對干預的畏懼心理所驅動。
根據日本央行的預測，其經常帳因財政因素預計減少 4,100 億日元，與貨幣經紀商估計的 7,000 億日元差距不大，遠低於 2022 年以來日本最小干預規模的 7,290 億日元，證實日本官方並未入市。
儘管如此，上月底美日聯手斥資 15.4 兆日元的歷史性干預，已徹底改變了交易員的心理防線。當日元兌美元再度逼近 160 大關時，畏懼干預的心理促使大量日元空頭部位在官方實際行動前便主動平倉。
更為關鍵且持久的支撐力道，來自於市場對日本央行貨幣政策升息路徑的重新定價。日本央行政策委員高田創日前發表鷹派演說，明確指出「2026年是貨幣政策的體制轉變」，並強調升息應是「敏捷且依據數據的」，不應受限於市場預期的固定間隔。
此發言直接挑戰了過往每半年調整一次的市場假設。目前隔夜指數交換(OIS)定價顯示，市場預期未來 12 個月將累計升息約 96.5 個基點，且 9 月升息的機率高達 84%。
此外，美國財政部長貝森特對日本政策正常化表達強烈支持，美日政策立場趨於一致，進一步削弱了市場放任日元過度貶值的信心。
paras_en: The yen‑dollar exchange rate experienced sharp volatility on Wednesday (the 2nd) and Thursday, climbing quickly from 160.38 and breaking through the 158 level, even touching a near‑one‑month high of 156.36 intraday. This rapid surge sparked heated market debate about whether the Japanese government would intervene in the FX market again.

However, the current‑account data released by the Bank of Japan (BOJ) showed no signs of large‑scale intervention this week. Analysts note that the move was not driven by direct official action but by traders re‑pricing expectations of BOJ rate hikes and a fear‑based mindset regarding possible intervention.

According to BOJ forecasts, the current account is expected to shrink by ¥410 billion due to fiscal factors, a figure close to the ¥700 billion estimate from currency dealers and far below the smallest intervention since 2022 of ¥729 billion, confirming that officials have not entered the market.

Nevertheless, the historic joint US‑Japan intervention at the end of last month, worth ¥15.4 trillion, has fundamentally altered traders’ psychological defenses. When the yen‑dollar pair again approached the 160 threshold, the fear of intervention prompted many short yen positions to be closed voluntarily before any official action materialised.

A more critical and lasting source of support comes from the market’s re‑pricing of the BOJ’s monetary‑policy tightening path. BOJ policy board member Hiroshi Takata recently delivered a hawkish speech, stating clearly that “2026 will be a structural shift in monetary policy,” and emphasizing that rate hikes should be “agile and data‑driven,” not constrained by fixed intervals dictated by market expectations.

His remarks directly challenge the long‑standing assumption of semi‑annual rate adjustments. Current overnight index swap (OIS) pricing indicates the market expects roughly 96.5 basis points of hikes over the next 12 months, with an 84% probability of a rate increase in September.

In addition, U.S. Treasury Secretary Vincent expressed strong support for Japan’s policy normalization, aligning U.S. and Japanese stances and further eroding market confidence in allowing the yen to depreciate excessively.

items.title: 全球機構投資人美元避險比率降至歷史新低 美元潛在拋售壓力巨大
items.title_en: Global Institutional Investors' Dollar Hedging Ratio Falls to Historic Low, Creating Massive Potential Dollar Sell Pressure
paras: 根據全球退休基金與保險公司最新申報資料，一些最龐大的美國資產持有者對美元走弱，幾乎沒有提供任何保護，這使得美元一旦面臨市場情緒逆轉，將面臨更急劇下跌的風險。
在包括日本、加拿大與台灣等六個主要市場中，截至今年6月30日，這些投資人對其外幣曝險僅進行了41%的避險，創下2015年以來的最低紀錄。這反映出隨著美元逐漸穩定，去年因川普政府關稅政策而急於規避美元損失的熱潮已然退去。

微幅調整避險比率 將引發數千億美元流動

Nuveen宏觀信用主管 Laura Cooper 表示：「鑑於外資持有美國資產的龐大規模，即便只是微幅調整避險比率，都可能引發顯著的外匯資金流動。」
根據彭博計算，這六個主要市場(還包含澳洲、丹麥與芬蘭)的外幣持有規模達4.6兆美元，避險比率只要提高5個百分點，就相當於高達2,300億美元的本國貨幣交易量。
Manulife投資管理多元資產方案投資長 Nathan Thooft 分析，若市場持續排除聯準會升息的可能性，且利差進一步收窄，投資人可能會開始重新建立避險部位，這將成為美元持續面臨賣壓的固定來源。

專家建議多元化資產配置

過去投資人減少避險是因為避險成本高昂，且相信美元在市場動盪時能發揮避險作用，藉此沖抵美國股債換回本國貨幣時的損失。然而，QIC多元資產方案主管 Stuart Simmons 警告，在政經不確定性升溫的時代，若仍過度依賴美元作為防禦手段，可能不再管用，他建議投資人應重新檢視並在海外資產組合中納入更多元的配置。
Equiti集團首席市場策略師 Noureldeen AlHammoury 指出，如果投資人不再確信美元能在市場恐慌時可靠地升值，就沒有理由繼續容忍龐大的未避險外幣曝險。
他補充說明，投資人並不需要拋售美股或美債，只需透過遠期外匯市場拋售美元來進行避險，這代表即使美國資產需求維持強勁，美元本身仍將面臨下行壓力。

日本可能成為集體避險的領頭羊

此波潛在的避險潮在亞洲及歐洲地區尤為關鍵。日本作為全球最大的美國公債海外持有國，避險需求可能最為迫切。
德意志銀行日本首席固定收益策略師Shoki Omori 表示，上一次避險比率如此低的時期是在2013年，當時美元正要開啟長達十年的多頭市場，而如今的總體經濟環境更像是當年的鏡像。
他預期，日本央行進一步升息收窄利差、美元急貶或壽險業新清償能力制度的推行，都可能成為觸發集體避險的催化劑。
paras_en: According to the latest filings from global pension funds and insurance companies, some of the largest holders of U.S. assets provide virtually no protection against a weakening dollar, meaning that if market sentiment reverses, the dollar could face a sharply accelerated decline.

Across six major markets—including Japan, Canada and Taiwan—by June 30 of this year these investors had hedged only 41% of their foreign‑currency exposure, the lowest level since 2015. This reflects that as the dollar has steadied, the rush last year to avoid dollar losses driven by the Trump administration’s tariff policies has faded.

A modest adjustment to the hedging ratio could trigger tens of billions of dollars of liquidity flows, says Laura Cooper, head of macro credit at Nuveen. "Given the massive scale of foreign holdings of U.S. assets, even a slight tweak in hedging ratios can generate significant foreign‑exchange capital movements," she said.

Bloomberg estimates that the foreign‑currency holdings in these six key markets (which also include Australia, Denmark and Finland) total $4.6 trillion. Raising the hedging ratio by just five percentage points would correspond to about $230 billion of domestic‑currency transactions.

Nathan Thooft, head of multi‑asset solutions at Manulife Investment Management, analyses that if markets continue to rule out further Fed rate hikes and yield spreads narrow further, investors may start rebuilding hedges, providing a persistent source of dollar‑selling pressure.

Experts advise diversifying asset allocations. In the past, investors reduced hedging because of high costs and the belief that the dollar would act as a safe haven during market turmoil, offsetting losses when U.S. equities and bonds were converted back to local currency. However, Stuart Simmons, head of multi‑asset solutions at QIC, warns that in an era of rising geopolitical uncertainty, over‑reliance on the dollar as a defensive tool may no longer work and recommends reassessing portfolios to include more diversified overseas allocations.

Equiti Group chief market strategist Noureldeen AlHammoury notes that if investors no longer trust the dollar to reliably appreciate during market panic, there is no reason to tolerate large un‑hedged foreign‑currency exposures.

He adds that investors do not need to sell U.S. stocks or bonds; they can hedge by selling dollars in the forward‑FX market, meaning that even if demand for U.S. assets stays strong, the dollar itself would still face downward pressure.

Japan could emerge as the leader of a collective hedging wave. This potential hedging surge is especially critical in Asia and Europe, and Japan, as the world’s largest foreign holder of U.S. Treasury bonds, may have the most urgent hedging needs.

Shoki Omori, chief fixed‑income strategist for Japan at Deutsche Bank, says the last time hedging ratios were this low was in 2013, when the dollar was about to embark on a decade‑long bull market, and today’s macro environment resembles a mirror image of that period.

He expects that further rate hikes by the Bank of Japan narrowing spreads, a rapid dollar depreciation, or the rollout of new solvency‑based regulations for life insurers could all act as catalysts triggering a collective hedging response.

items.title_en: US Bonds Raise Alarm! Overseas US Asset Hedging Ratio Hits Ten-Year Low; Experts Say Depreciation Trades Are Heating Up, and a Dollar Collapse Could Trigger Continuous Liquidations
paras: 外媒最新報導出，根據日本、加拿大、台灣、澳洲、丹麥及芬蘭等六地退休基金與保險公司申報文件，截至今年6月30日，海外投資人持有美股美債的外幣曝險避險比率僅約41%，創2015年來新低。
去年川普推出全球關稅、美元急貶時，上述避險比率曾短暫跳升，但這股熱潮隨著美元回穩、避險成本居高不下而迅速消退，投資人重回「波動時美元自動避險」的舊策略，也就是靠美元升值緩衝本幣計價的美國資產回撤，省下昂貴的衍生品費用。
但美元本季跌約2%、兌多數G10貨幣走弱，「貶值交易」(debasement trade)重新升溫，加上美日聯手干預日元、美國財政部擴大長債回購來壓抑殖利率，加上市場質疑聯準會(Fed)主席華許會否真升息抗通膨，均加劇「美國政策侵蝕美元」的敘事。
匯率避險是利用衍生性商品賣出美元、買進投資人本國貨幣，以防範匯率波動。由於美國資產在全球投資組合中佔有很大比重，增加避險其實意味著更多美元賣盤。
管理1.4兆美元的Nuveen宏觀信貸主管Laura Coope指出，海外持美資產規模龐大，避險比率只需小幅上調，就能撬動可觀外匯流量。根據測算，上述六地合計4.6兆美元外幣部位中，避險比率每上升5個百分點，等於約2300億美元交易量。
雖然上述估算未納入英國和歐元區等主要市場，但所涵蓋國家仍占美國資產海外持有量相當大的一部分。日本是全球最大的美國國債海外持有國，佔外國持有量約10%，加拿大和台灣也高居前十名。
paras_en: Foreign media reports that, based on filing documents from pension funds and insurance companies in Japan, Canada, Taiwan, Australia, Denmark and Finland, the foreign‑currency hedging ratio for overseas investors’ US equity and US Treasury holdings was only about 41% as of June 30 this year, a new low not seen since 2015.

Last year, when President Trump rolled out global tariffs and the dollar sharply depreciated, the hedging ratio briefly spiked, but the rally faded quickly as the dollar steadied and hedging costs remained high. Investors reverted to the old “automatic dollar hedge in volatile times” approach—relying on a stronger dollar to cushion the pull‑back of US‑denominated assets priced in local currencies and saving on expensive derivatives fees.

However, the dollar has fallen roughly 2% this quarter and weakened against most G10 currencies, reviving “debasement trades.” Combined with coordinated US‑Japan intervention in the yen, the US Treasury’s expanded long‑bond buybacks to suppress yields, and market doubts about whether Fed Chair Jerome Powell will truly raise rates to combat inflation, the narrative that “US policy is eroding the dollar” has intensified.

Currency hedging uses derivatives to sell dollars and buy the investor’s home currency to guard against exchange‑rate swings. Because US assets make up a large share of global portfolios, increasing hedges actually means more dollar selling pressure.

Laura Coope, head of macro credit at Nuveen, which manages $1.4 trillion, notes that overseas holdings of US assets are massive, and a modest uptick in the hedging ratio could mobilise a sizable FX flow. Her calculations show that among the six jurisdictions, the combined $4.6 trillion foreign‑currency exposure would generate about $230 billion of transaction volume for each 5‑percentage‑point rise in the hedging ratio.

Although the estimate excludes major markets such as the UK and the euro‑area, the covered countries still represent a substantial share of overseas US‑asset holdings. Japan is the world’s largest foreign holder of US Treasury bonds, accounting for roughly 10% of foreign holdings, with Canada and Taiwan also ranking among the top ten.
